chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: The big band with Eddie Durham at Bridgeport
summary: Smith and Eddie Durham took a band to a boardwalk dance hall in Bridgeport for two summers, with many Smiths and arrangers.

bands.name: Eddie Durham and Buster Smith's band

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: No, no. Eddie Durham and I made up a big band and take it up... For two years we took it up to Bridgeport, Connecticut, and played up there all summer out on the walk. The man had a big dance hall right out on the boardwalk there. And we stayed up there and played up there.
Was it by the sea?
Mmm-hmm.
What kind of a dancehall was it?
Just a plain dance hall. A White dance hall. They didn't have no drinks, serve no drinks or nothin' in there. Just a regular dancehall, give dances three or four hours.
Every night?
About six nights a week.
And presumably the Swing thing was on by then -- the Swing craze.
Yeah.
So everybody wanted you to play Swing music.
Yeah.
Were you still expected to play waltzes and that kind of stuff?
Yeah, we had to play waltzes up there.
But they liked the exciting numbers, too.
Oh yeah. That was your main repertory. You had
Buster Smith - 162
to have a lot of Swing music.
Were you writing the arrangements for that band as well?

Two or three. Eddie Durham and Ben Smith -- three or four arrangers in there. I think the guitar player, he arranged some, and then Eddie Durham did the most arranging, and Ben Smith did a lot of arranging.
He was an alto player, too.
Yeah.
Who else was in the band? Do you remember?
Let's see. Ike Quebec and Tab Smith, Ben Smith...
Buster Smith?
Yeah.
Three Smiths in the saxophone section!
Four Smiths. The drummer was a Smith. Yeah.
The trumpets?
We had Joe Guy on the trumpet, and I can't think of the other Joe... There were three Joe's on the trumpet. Joe Keyes, Joe Guy and this other Joe.
Not Joe Wilder.

Might be. A tall dark boy. And we had trombones... Let me see who was in the trombones. Eddie Durham and we had...I forget the other boys on trombone. I forget their name. And we had a Smitty on drums. He was a crippled fellow. Let me see... Who was playing piano? We had 17 pieces.
Buster Smith - 163
That's a big band.
Mmm-hmm, yeah. 17 pieces.
And this was just for a summer vacation thing...?
Yeah.
